claim: New York has no general statute governing or prohibiting employment non-competes; enforceability is governed by common-law caselaw applying a reasonableness standard.
evidence: In New York State, there is currently no statute that prohibits restrictive covenants between employers and employees, and or limits them in any way. Instead, there is a robust set of decisions and case law – aka law that is based on precedents from prior cases rather than based on constitutions, statutes, and/or regulations – which has been developed through New York courts. The standard which courts look to govern all restrictive covenants in New York is the reasonableness standard.
excerpt: Restrictive Covenants – typically Non-Competition or Non-Solicitation clauses in employment contracts – are a binding agreement between the employer and the employee that is meant to prevent unfair competition by limiting the employee’s job or business activities after their employment ends.
